title: Identification of core differentially expressed genes for respiratory syncytial virus infection.
summary: Integrating transcriptomic differential analysis, WGCNA and machine learning yielded eight RSV-associated feature genes from patient blood-expression data; an external GEO dataset and qRT-PCR in 9 patients/3 controls supported selected expression findings, particularly RETN. The results identify candidate biomarkers and do not establish causality, clinical diagnostic performance, or therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: WGCNA identified correlated modules; LASSO cross-validation and random-forest feature importance filtered candidate hub genes to eight RSV-associated genes, with RF evaluated on an independent GEO test dataset.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: The analysis selected eight feature genes; RETN and ARG1 also had colocalization signals with lower respiratory tract infection. The paper reports 72% test-set RF accuracy and candidate-gene expression differences.
evidence.unknown: GSE38900 (28 RSV, 8 controls) was the independent dataset; expression patterns were assessed there. qRT-PCR in 9 RSV patients and 3 healthy controls significantly supported RETN; this small assay does not validate a clinical test or causal mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: WGCNA identified correlated modules; LASSO cross-validation and random-forest feature importance filtered candidate hub genes to eight RSV-associated genes, with RF evaluated on an independent GEO test dataset.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
